decisionsTitle: Every mail goes through the outbox, and one road down is no loss: why Gmail «did not send» on QA, the visitors' messages queued, failover between Mailgun and Gmail (amending §149, §676, §772 and §622)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-15, ~10:05**, with a screenshot of «Setări» → «Spune-ne ceva» on QA, all four forms set to Mailgun: «aici nu se trimiteau mailurile prin Gmail-ul clubului… nu înțeleg de ce, dar mergea doar cu Mailgun. Vreau să mă asigur că 1: există un queue de mailuri de trimis și nu se pierd mesaje; 2: dacă pică un serviciu (Mailgun) se trimite prin celălalt (Gmail) și invers.» He had said «YOLO» the day before: the open points below are decided, and said.

**The diagnosis, first (read-only: `vercel api` for the env names, `vercel logs` on both projects, `/api/health?deep=1` on QA).** Gmail did not fail. QA has `CONTACT_SMTP_USER` and `CONTACT_SMTP_PASSWORD` (so the card did not grey the road), and its function log from 2026-10-14 19:05 to 2026-10-15 06:52 UTC holds eight posts to `/ro/contact/spune-ne`, every one `[feedback] <form> <reader>: sent` — the service logs `sent` only when Nodemailer reports an accepted recipient, i.e. Google answered 250 — and not one `[feedback] delivery failed` or `smtp <code>` line in seven days. The same account carries the outbox on QA: `email.gmail` reads configured, twenty sent in the last day, last failure `smtp ETIMEDOUT` on 2026-09-28, nothing since. **So no 535-5.7.8, no wrong port, no egress block, no unset variable.** What the site could not say is *where the accepted message went*: the direct sender logged `sent` and kept nothing — no road, no id, no time. The most likely reason a message Gmail accepted was not seen is that the form's «Către» was the club's own Gmail (the account that sends): Gmail keeps a message From = To in Sent / All mail and not necessarily in the Inbox — not provable from outside (the addresses are in the database), so the card now warns beside the box, and the owner is told how to check in a minute. A second difference is gone too: the direct Gmail send never consulted QA's allowlist while Mailgun's road did. **Production's «Scrie-ne» is not losing messages to a refusal:** same variables, two contact posts in seven days, both accepted (`[contact] delivered marked as possible spam`), no failure line; the same «Către = the sending account» risk applies to it.

**Decision.** (1) **One outbox for every mail.** «Scrie-ne» (§149) and the four «Spune-ne ceva» forms (§676, §772) no longer send from the request. Each queues an outbox row — three new message types, `CONTACT_MESSAGE`, `FEEDBACK_MESSAGE` and the platform's own `RELAY_NOTICE`, and three expand-only columns on `email_outbox` (migration `0161_outbox_road_and_failures`: `road`, the club's choice for the form; `road_failures`, what each road did to this message; `body_deleted_at`) — and answers «trimis»; the same request sends it after its response (`drainRelayAfterResponse`, whatever «Când pleacă emailurile» says, up to four passes in thirty seconds), the outbox job sends what is left. A visitor's message has its own worker (`notifications/relay.ts`) and the notifications' claim leaves it alone: it has no template, no participant and a road of its own. The contact form's row carries the club's To, the other recipients as visible copies and the Bcc list; a «Spune-ne ceva» message is one row per recipient. (2) **The words are kept until delivery, never after.** The words travel in `payload_json`; the moment the message leaves they are deleted (`{ "deleted": true }`, `body_deleted_at`) and the row stays as the record — road, road it left by, time, provider id, tries, what each road answered; never an address or a word. So «the site keeps nothing» became «the site keeps a message only until it is delivered, seconds, never after»: the card's footer, the forms' sentences (`Tell.safety.reader*`, `Tell.privacy*`), `Admin.emails.feedbackForms.roads` and the privacy notice **template**'s contact and feedback paragraphs now say it (template only: the texts in force move when the club approves; until then the notice in force says «nicio copie», which is untrue for the seconds a row waits — the notice is on the list to approve again, and the owner decides whether to wait for that before the release: see the questions). The anonymous forms stay anonymous: nothing of the sender beyond what the message carries is stored, and the row is cleaned the same way. (3) **Failover, both ways.** A failure that is the SERVICE's — a refused login (`smtp EAUTH`, Mailgun 401/403), a 5xx, no connection, a spent allowance or a pause — counts against the road for that message; after **two** (decided: one is a hiccup, a second a minute later is a road down) the other road gets its turn, Mailgun to Gmail and Gmail to Mailgun, and the two take turns by their counts after that. The first retries are three and five seconds, so the after-response pass reaches the other road within seconds; then the outbox's own backoff. A road this deployment lacks, or that Mailgun has stopped (§605, §622), is skipped at once. The row says «Trimis prin cealaltă cale»; a line `[email-relay] … left by gmail` goes to the function log (the house's operations log), an audit row `email_road.failed_over` names the roads (no actor, never a word or an address), and each Administrator and Superadministrator is emailed once a day per road (`RELAY_NOTICE`, composed in RO or EN by the person's own language). (4) **Never a double send.** A refused address is the recipient's, not the road's: BOUNCED, the other road is not tried, the Administrators are told. A send whose connection broke where the service may already have the message is *ambiguous* and **pins the message to that road** — retried there only, never handed over: nothing can say whether Gmail or Mailgun delivered a message whose answer never came (Gmail has no lookup, Mailgun's id is exactly what was lost), so the state of an ambiguous send is never known and the message does not change road; one idempotency key per message rides both roads (`X-Outbox-Key`, `v:idempotency_key`). To make that distinction real the adapters say what they know: a Gmail timeout or socket error before `DATA` (the 2026-09-28 `ETIMEDOUT`, a connect or greeting that never answered) is no longer ambiguous, Mailgun's `fetch` failures are ambiguous unless the request certainly never reached it (DNS, refused, connect timeout), and both roads now honour `replyTo`, `replyToName` and `noReplyTo` (Gmail ignored them for the outbox). (5) **Girl Zone.** A message for her person that Mailgun cannot carry goes by Gmail only if the club ticked «Dacă Mailgun pică, trimite prin Gmail-ul clubului» on «Pagini» → «Contact» (a real tick, off by default, with the note that whoever reads the club's mailbox sees it in Sent; stored in the setting's JSON, `safety.fallbackToGmail`, audited) AND the privacy notice in force names Gmail for her messages (`{{feedbackSafetyGmail}}`): the tick is greyed with its reason until it does, and an unticked message waits for Mailgun — never by the club's mailbox. Her message by the Gmail the club chose for her may be taken over by Mailgun, the road the notice promised her. The contact form and the three ordinary forms fall back by default. (6) **A day without a road.** A transient refusal is never the end of an ordinary email (§622), but this is somebody's words in a table: after twenty-four hours the message is FAILED, its words deleted, the Administrators emailed («Un mesaj de pe site nu a putut fi trimis»), an audit row `email_relay.lost` written; «Reîncearcă emailurile eșuate» does not put it back (nothing is left to send) and `/api/health` does not count it as `failed` (a 503 nothing can clear for a week) — it has its own «Sarcini» row for seven days. (7) **The roads' state.** `platform_settings.emailRoadStatus` holds, per road, since when it has been failing and its last short error code (written only on a failure and when a failing road works again, by the notifications' sender too — `withRoadStatus`); the last success is read from the outbox. `/devs` → «Stare» shows each road's last success and last refusal; «Setări» → «Emailuri» → «Mesaje de pe site» shows both and one row per message of the last seven days with its road, how it left, its tries, the words' state; `/admin/tasks` carries the red rows `emailRoadDown` (a road failing over an hour) and `relayLost`. (8) **One rule for both roads on QA.** The environment's allowlist now judges Gmail's road as Mailgun's: a recipient it does not name is captured, with 0 recipients on the row. The contact form's Gmail messages also count against Gmail's daily cap (§443), like every outbox row.

**Kept.** The outbox table, its claim and send path for the twenty-seven notification types, the Mailgun stop and the Gmail fallback (§622), Gmail's cap and pace (§443), the canonicalizer, hashed single-use links, `APP_BASE_URL` for every address, no new dependency (Nodemailer and the Mailgun `fetch` adapter as they were), no legal text in effect changed.

**Rejected.** Sending the message first and queueing only a failure — it would leave `/admin/emails` blind to the happy path, which is what hid the cause. A second table for visitors' messages — the owner asked for one outbox. Looking a message up at Gmail or Mailgun to resolve an ambiguous send — Gmail has no API for it from SMTP, and Mailgun's logs key is a developer's, not the app's. Failing over on a bounce — the other road would bounce the same address and a second provider would see a bad recipient. Keeping the words after a failure «for the Administrators to resend» — the notice promises seconds, and the owner's own wording was «se șterge». A marker in the privacy notice to gate the queue — twenty-two files for the sake of a clause that says what the code does for seconds; the lawyer reads the sentence when the club approves.

**Decided by the dispatcher on the owner's «YOLO»** (the owner may overturn): two failures before the other road; twenty-four hours before a message is given up on; an ambiguous send never changes road; the allowlist applies to Gmail; failed messages are not part of `/api/health`'s `failed`; the Administrators' notices are emails composed by the relay (no new template in the email editor); the contact form stays Gmail-first.

**Amends** §149 (the contact form's message is an outbox row, no longer sent from the request and never kept nowhere), §676 and §772 (the forms' delivery and the card's footer: kept only until delivered; a road is the club's choice, and the other road carries it when it is down), §622 (the Administrators' notice and the «Sarcini» rows for a road that is down, and the transient-refusal rule's one exception: a visitor's message is given up on after a day), §443 (the contact form's messages count against Gmail's cap; the adapter reads a timeout before `DATA` as not accepted) and §68 (a visitor's message leaves after its response whatever the delivery timing).

**Tests.** Unit `road-failover.test.ts` (the rule as a table: failover after two, both ways, turns, the pin, the stopped road, what each answer means), `relay-adapters.test.ts` (the Gmail timeout before and during `DATA`, the Reply-To of both roads, Mailgun's request that never reached it), `feedback-fallback-tick.test.ts` (the tick, greyed and carried, the self-recipient warning, `fallbackAllowedFor`), `owner-tasks.test.ts` (the two rows), the i18n guards. Integration `notifications/relay.test.ts` (PGlite: queue and deliver, the words gone; Mailgun to Gmail and back with the mark, the audit row, the log line and the notices in both languages; a 401 as a service failure; a spent allowance as all attempts at once; a stopped road skipped; a bounce ends BOUNCED with no other road; an ambiguous send never leaves its road; Girl Zone without the tick never leaves Mailgun; Gmail's pace is no failure; twenty-four hours; a notice raises none; the main claim, «Reîncearcă…» and `/api/health` leave it alone; the page's read has no address or word), `notifications/road-status.test.ts`, `feedback/submit.test.ts` and `contact/*.test.ts` (the services queue; the relay delivers; refused roads answer «sent»; the tick saved, audited, kept when greyed). E2E `feedback.spec.ts` and `contact.spec.ts` through the outbox and the capture sink.
changelogLine: - **«Scrie-ne» and «Spune-ne ceva» through the outbox, with failover** — a visitor's message is queued, sent at once after the response, and carried by the other road (Gmail or Mailgun) when the chosen one fails twice; its words are deleted the moment it leaves, a refused address is never retried elsewhere and a send that may already be delivered never changes road; Girl Zone falls back to Gmail only with the club's tick; «Mesaje de pe site», `/devs` and «Sarcini» show each road's state, and the Administrators are emailed when a road is down or a message is lost. QA's «did not send by Gmail» was Gmail accepting every message: §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Amends criteria 3, 6, 27, 28 and 29. Given a valid post of «Scrie-ne» or of any «Spune-ne ceva» form, when the action answers, then the message is one row of `email_outbox` (type `CONTACT_MESSAGE` or `FEEDBACK_MESSAGE`, no participant, no registration) carrying the road the club chose in `road` and its words in `payload_json`, answered «trimis» whatever the road does next, and sent after the response by the relay (`notifications/relay.ts`), never from the request; on delivery the words are deleted (`payload_json` = `{"deleted":true}`, `body_deleted_at` set) and the row keeps its road, the road it left by, the time and the provider's id, and no address or word of any message (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a visitor's message whose chosen road has failed it twice with a failure that is the service's (a refused login, a 5xx, no connection, a spent allowance or a pause) — never the recipient's — when the relay next sends it, then the other road carries it, both ways, Mailgun to Gmail and Gmail to Mailgun, once the other road is configured and not stopped; the row's `transport` differs from its `road` and the page says «Trimis prin cealaltă cale», one function-log line and one `email_road.failed_over` audit row (no actor, no word, no address) are written, and every Administrator and Superadministrator is emailed once a day per road in the language of their own row (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a refused recipient address the message ends BOUNCED and no other road is tried; given a failure after which the service may already have the message (a timeout or a dropped socket once the message was on its way), the message is pinned to that road and is retried there only, never by the other, and one idempotency key rides both roads; given a visitor's message no road has carried in twenty-four hours, it is FAILED, its words are deleted, the Administrators are emailed and an `email_relay.lost` audit row is written, and «Reîncearcă emailurile eșuate» does not put it back (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given Girl Zone's person as the reader, when Mailgun cannot carry her message, then it goes by Gmail only while the club's tick «Dacă Mailgun pică, trimite prin Gmail-ul clubului» is on (a checkbox, off by default, with the note that the club's mailbox readers see the message in Sent, greyed with its reason and keeping what is saved while Gmail is missing or the notice in force does not name `{{feedbackSafetyGmail}}`) AND that notice names it; otherwise it waits for Mailgun, and the other three forms and the contact form fall back by default (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given «Setări» → «Emailuri», `/devs` → «Stare» and «Sarcini», when they render, then «Mesaje de pe site» lists the visitors' messages of the last seven days with their form, status, road chosen, road they left by, tries, what each road answered and whether the words are kept or deleted — no address and no word — beside each road's last success, last refusal and, while failing, since when; `/devs` shows the same per road; and «Sarcini» carries the red rows `emailRoadDown` (a road failing for over an hour, named with its last code) and `relayLost` (a message given up on in seven days), both in Romanian and English (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a form whose recipient is the very Gmail account that sends (by the canonicalizer, never a string compare) and whose road is Gmail, when «Pagini» → «Contact» renders, then a warning beside the recipient says Gmail may keep such a message in Sent only; the privacy notice template's contact and feedback paragraphs say the platform keeps a message only until it leaves and deletes it, and that the other road carries it when the chosen one is down, in both languages (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 1. The outbox also carries the visitors' messages (`CONTACT_MESSAGE`, `FEEDBACK_MESSAGE`) and the platform's own notices about a road (`RELAY_NOTICE`) through a worker of their own: the notifications' claim never takes them, `/api/health` counts them as waiting and, after ninety minutes, overdue, but not as `failed`, and the road each row asked for, the failures each road gave it and the deletion of its words are columns of `email_outbox` (migration `0161_outbox_road_and_failures`, expand only) (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a Gmail connection or greeting that never answered, or a socket error before the SMTP `DATA` command, when the Gmail road reports it, then it is a failure before acceptance — the sender hands the message to Mailgun at once for a group the club put on Gmail — and an error during `DATA` or with no command named stays "may have been accepted"; given a Mailgun request that never reached it (DNS, refused, connect timeout) the result is not ambiguous, and any other network failure is (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: every mail through the outbox; failover between Mailgun and Gmail
